newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Student protests over austerity heat up in Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: Student protests over austerity heat up in Ecuador.

text.p: Ecuador suspended classes in Quito schools on Wednesday as clashes between students and police continued over economic cutbacks.

Television showed police entering Central University premises to arrest protesters, violating regulations that ban them from the campus. High school and university students said they would march on Congress on Thursday to request a halt to President Abdala Bucaram's austerity drive that hikes the costs of services such as fuel, electricity and telephones.

University Students Federation (FEUE) president Patricio Carrera told Reuters 15 organisations backed the march, expected to number 300,000, called by FEUE, the High School Students Federation (FESE) and the Revolutionary Youth (JRE), including human rights and environmental groups.

Carrera said students would also urge the resignation of the ministers of education and energy, Sandra Correa and Alfredo Adum, and would ask Congress to grill Government Minister Frank Vargas "on the violent action of police."
On Tuesday one student leader was hit by a bullet and a teenager lost his eye when a tear gas bomb burst in his face.
"Police invade university premises and hurl tear gas bombs against the bodies of students. We have videos," Carrera said.
A police spokesman denied the charges.
So far nine policemen and 20 students have been injured and at least 150 people detained in protests.
Bucaram decreed rises in electricity rates of 235 percent for homes, 77 percent for shops and 53 percent for industries.
Ecuador's trade unions are mulling a general strike for Feb. 5 to protest the tariff rises.
